It is that score exactly, on the same fixture, by the same mechanism, and it is the number docs/detector-capabilities.md has carried since the 2026-06-13 post-H7 re-baseline. theResultThatMatters.whatTheModelActuallySaid: READ, not inferred, per the rule that lane membership may be cited from the census but a verdict's correctness may not be cited without reading it. On all four MEDIUM runs the model's stated reason for MEDIUM rather than HIGH is the same: the withAccountApiKey wrapper plausibly authenticates the caller (so the confidence is hedged), but the handler body applies no ownership or scope filter, so any authenticated caller can delete any label. The hedge is about the wrapper; the finding is about the missing scope filter. That is a correct and well-reasoned uncertainty, and the pre-#152 policy discarded it.

censusFidelityDefect.headline: THE RECORDED-VERDICT CENSUS WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE OUTCOME AND WRONG ABOUT THE MECHANISM, AND n=1 GIVES NO SIGNAL ABOUT WHICH FIXTURE IS THE EXCEPTION.
censusFidelityDefect.whatWasRecorded: The single n=1 replay recording for positive/15 (fixtures/replay/auth-bypass-multi/be1492ec3c4575569cd32c04220c74e75c3ed6d9a3a60fe9aa58f6fbaf0255d6.json) is isVulnerable true at confidence high. READ from the file, not inferred from the census summary.

measuredFidelityOfTheWholeCorpus.derivation: 22 positives x 5 = 110 vulnerable assertions = 106 vuln/high + 4 vuln/medium; the 4 mediums are positive/15 runs 1-4 and its run 5 is high, so the other 21 positives are 105/105 vuln/high. 15 model-reaching negatives x 5 = 75 = 70 safe/high + 5 safe/low, and all five safe/low runs are negative/14, matching its recording. censusFidelityDefect.whyThatIsTheDangerousResult: 97.3% fixture-level fidelity is high enough to be trusted and does not identify its own exception. The census was not unreliable in general; it was wrong in exactly one place, and n=1 cannot say where.
censusFidelityDefect.THE_DIVERGENCE_WAS_CONFIDENCE_ONLY_AND_T: positive/15 held isVulnerable TRUE on all five runs; only its confidence moved. Decomposed, the census's SIGN fidelity across this run is 37 of 37 and its CONFIDENCE fidelity is 36 of 37. Nothing in 185 calls changed a recorded sign.
censusFidelityDefect.soTheNegativeCounterfactualDOESNOTFOLLOW: CORRECTING A CLAIM THIS RECORD INITIALLY MADE, AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS. Transposing this run's divergence onto a NEGATIVE does NOT produce a red. scoreNegative ignores confidence entirely, so a negative whose recording reads safe/high and whose live behaviour is safe/medium still passes 5/5 clean and seeds no declaration. The observed error class is harmless on negatives BY CONSTRUCTION, not by luck. Any claim that this run shows n=1 seeding could have returned a full RED is overstated and must not be cited.
censusFidelityDefect.whatOptionCACTUALLYABSORBED: Under the shipped policy a MEDIUM positive still flags, so the confidence divergence was harmless on the positive side too. Negatives were always scored on sign, and option C makes a positive's fate turn on sign rather than on confidence, so the one observed error class is now harmless on BOTH sides. Under the RETIRED policy that same error is exactly what produced 44/45. The safety is a property of option C, not a property of the census.
censusFidelityDefect.theResidualThatIsGENUINELYUNMEASURED: A SIGN divergence from an n=1 seed. That is the only class that can red a run, and this run produced zero instances of it, so it supplies no estimate of its frequency. 37 of 37 at n=5 bounds it loosely and does not exclude it. The honest residual is therefore narrower than 'n=1 can red a run': it is that n=1 cannot distinguish a faithful sign from a lucky one, and this run did not test that, because no sign moved.
censusFidelityDefect.recommendation: Do not seed declarations from n=1 without stating that the seed is n=1, and state the sign/confidence split when doing so, since only the sign half can fail a gate. This does not argue for re-recording at n>1, which spends real money and overwrites frozen evidence.

RESOLUTION_2026_08_10.TRANSFERABLE_RULE_readThisBeforeAuthorin: WARNING, NOT A NOTE. If your prediction reads ANY property off an n=1 recording - sign, confidence, lane membership, cost - you are predicting the MODAL branch and nothing whatever about WHICH fixture is the exception. The record already said so before this run: #155 measured 36 of 37 fixtures reproducing their recording at n=5 and exactly one not, and concluded that n=1 gives no signal about which is the exception. This block applied that reasoning to CONFIDENCE, argued it explicitly and at length, and then predicted SIGN per fixture from the same n=1 seeds without noticing the argument transferred. The property changed; the blindness did not. Do NOT write a per-fixture prediction of any n=1-derived property unless you also record which fixtures could be the exception and what happens if one is. On a corpus with zero slack, exactly one exception is a full RED, so 'probably all of them' is not a prediction, it is a coin toss with the whole gate on it.
RESOLUTION_2026_08_10.aReRunBeforeAdjudicationIsAGuaranteedRED: negative/08 returned isVulnerable on 5 of 5 runs, so it is STABLE and not marginal, and no fixture has been touched. 'Exit 2 consumes the authorization' must NOT be read by a later session as 'a re-run merely needs fresh money.' Spending on a result that is decided before the dispatch is the same shape as a gate hardcoded above the enumerated corpus, which this project nearly paid for once. The next env-exposure dispatch is justified only AFTER L-016 is adjudicated and whatever follows from that adjudication has landed.
RESOLUTION_2026_08_10.evidenceAboutTheDETECTOR_notAboutTheGate: All SEVEN negatives that fully satisfy a written reject clause scored clean 5/5: negative/01 (admin auth AND production 404 AND curated subset), negative/02, negative/05, negative/09 and negative/10 (allowlisted non-secret values only), negative/06 (env routed through a pino redacting logger, never to a response), and negative/04 (key NAMES only AND 404 in production - both conjuncts). RESOLUTION_2026_08_10.promptVersusCorpus_FILED_AS_L016: The disagreement is real, its extent is measured, and it is NOT adjudicated here. EXTENT: exactly ONE fixture, negative/08-flask-env-keys-only.py. The names-only shape exists in exactly two files corpus-wide and both are negatives: negative/04 returns Object.keys(process.env).sort() and 404s in production; negative/08 returns sorted(os.environ.keys()) with no authentication, authorization or production guard of any kind. positive/10-go-env-dump.go touches os.Environ() but splits on '=' and returns names AND values, so it is not the same shape. THE DISAGREEMENT, stated as a fact about two artifacts: the corpus labels BOTH the guarded and the unguarded names-only case as negative, while the detector's rejection clause ('Reject when only env KEY NAMES are returned (no values), and the route is dev-only / 404 in production') is a CONJUNCTION that distinguishes them. The corpus does not treat the guard as load-bearing; the prompt does. Separately, the prompt's opening definition scopes the harm to values being returned, which points the other way on this one input and never functions as a rejection ground anywhere else in the corpus. WHICH HALF IS AUTHORITATIVE IS NOT DECIDED HERE and is not the resolution's to decide: R8 and R11 forbid editing a prompt to make a verdict come out right, and the stop-and-report rule forbids fixing an unexpected verdict in the same execution. Filed as L-016. No fixture was edited, relabelled or moved.

costBand.howTheWideningWasCHOSEN_notDerived: READ THIS BEFORE RE-EXECUTING THE ARITHMETIC. The band spans both anchors and is widened by -19.0% / +17.0%: 0.6649 x 0.81 = $0.5386 low, 0.7038 x 1.17 = $0.8234 high. That envelope is the FLAT CONSTANT's prediction error across six paid runs, and its source is flatConstantErrorUpdate IN THIS FILE, not the perRun table. It is NOT a measurement of run-to-run variation of one detector on one corpus, which is the quantity anchor A actually depends on. That quantity has ZERO observations, because no detector has ever been re-run, so no envelope belonging to anchor A exists to derive. The magnitude is therefore BORROWED and CHOSEN, not computed. It is kept rather than dropped because with no widening the band is $0.6649-$0.7038 and the ceiling would have to sit just above $0.70, where it could fire on a legitimate result, and a ceiling that can fire on a legitimate result is a coin toss on our own hypothesis rather than a guard.

threeExits.why: Stated inside the artifact rather than assumed from precedent, because this artifact is what a later reader has.
threeExits.1_success: 20/20. Consumes the authorization. F-004's sixth per-detector green.
threeExits.2_detectionFailure: Any score below 20/20. CONSUMES the authorization and does NOT earn a re-run. Re-sampling is a fresh decision requiring fresh authorization.
threeExits.3_abortOnCeiling: SpendCeilingExceeded at $1.00. Does NOT consume the authorization, but BOUNDED: one retry only, cumulative spend across attempts counted and reported, and a SECOND abort escalates to fresh authorization rather than a third attempt. Without that bound a dollar authorization becomes an unlimited one, since every abort spends up to the ceiling.
threeExits.transportFailure: Treated as exit 3 under the same bound. It spends the same dollars.

claimsUNAVAILABLE_regardlessOfOutcome.spendCeiling: #148's ceiling has never executed live. test:spend-ceiling is keyless and sits in the test:ci chain, so the PREDICATE is gated for free on every push; what is untested is a live abort against real accumulating spend. No run may be cited as evidence for the live path unless the abort actually fires, and no abort will be engineered to obtain it.
claimsUNAVAILABLE_regardlessOfOutcome.simultaneity: A sixth green at a sixth SHA does not prove the six pass simultaneously at one SHA.
claimsUNAVAILABLE_regardlessOfOutcome.calibration: R3 forbids reading zero false positives at n=5 as calibration.

preRegisteredEnvExposureRerun_2026_08_10.procedure: The proven stage-3 dispatch procedure, unchanged: validate the key out of band, set it by hand in the UI, verify main SHA plus required checks plus zero secrets and variables plus no run in flight, dispatch EXACTLY ONCE, delete the secret the moment the run step goes terminal, verify 404 and total_count 0. Guard 1 asserts key PRESENCE, never VALIDITY.
